questions.question: Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. (CO3; A) Reading Passage 1 Music has long been recognised as more than just entertainment. In recent years, researchers have explored its impact on mental and physical health. Listening to calming music has been shown to reduce stress levels, lower blood pressure and improve sleep quality. In hospitals, certain types of music are used to help patients relax before surgery or cope with pain during recovery. Music therapy, a structured form of treatment, is now offered in many healthcare settings to support emotional well-being. While not a replacement for medical care, music is increasingly viewed as a valuable complement to traditional treatment methods. a. What is the main idea of the passage? b. How does music affect physical health, according to the passage? c. What is music therapy and where is it used? d. Why is music not considered a replacement for medical care? e. What can be inferred about the role of music in hospitals? Reading Passage 2 Advancements in medical technology have transformed the way healthcare is delivered, but they also raise complex ethical questions. For instance, artificial intelligence is now capable of assisting in diagnosis, predicting patient outcomes and even guiding surgical procedures. While these innovations promise greater accuracy and efficiency, they also challenge traditional roles of medical professionals. Some experts worry that over-reliance on machines may reduce human judgment in critical situations. Others argue that technology can enhance decision- making when used responsibly. As hospitals adopt more automated systems, the balance between human care and machine precision becomes a central concern. Ultimately, the goal is not to replace doctors, but to support them in providing better care. f. How is artificial intelligence being used in healthcare? g. What ethical concern is raised about relying on machines? h. What can be inferred about the writer’s opinion on replacing doctors with machines? i. Why might some experts be cautious about increased automation in hospitals? j. How does the passage reflect both optimism and concern about medical technology? Reading Passage 3 Training in sports increasingly includes young-athlete neuromuscular (PNM) development, which focuses on stretching, balance, and muscle awareness. Schools and academies adopt apps like the Hudl to review movement and progress. These tools improve flexibility and reduce injury, but some coaches worry that screens may distract from real-field observation. Others feel technology can guide better training if limited and monitored. The aim is to improve athletes, not science itself. k. What is the focus of PNM development in sports training? l. How are schools using sports technology in athlete training? m. What concern do some coaches raise about using screens during sports training? n. What is the writer’s opinion on technology replacing traditional coaching? o. What is the main goal of combining PNM development and technology? (1×15=15)

• Practical Applications & Critical Evaluation (2 Marks): Real-world applications, computational complexity, empirical validation, or critical critique.
• Conclusion & Summary (1 Mark): Concise synthesis connecting theoretical outcomes with course objectives.
